title: What If You Held In Every Sneeze?

scenes.text: What if you held in every sneeze? The pressure has to go somewhere.
A sneeze is a blast of air from your lungs. Pinch your nose and shut your mouth, and it's trapped inside.
Doctors say that can push the pressure in your airway to more than 20 times a normal sneeze.
In 2023, a man in Dundee, Scotland, did exactly that while driving with hay fever.
Air leaked under the skin of his neck. Scans found a two millimetre tear in his windpipe, the first known case.
It healed in five weeks without surgery. His doctors' advice to everyone: never stop a sneeze by pinching your nose.

description:
What if you held in every sneeze? Pinching your nose and closing your mouth can raise the pressure in your airway to more than 20 times that of a normal sneeze.
In 2023 a man in Dundee tore a 2 mm hole in his windpipe doing exactly that, the first known case. He needed no surgery; a scan five weeks later showed it had healed. His doctors, writing in BMJ Case Reports, advised against stifling sneezes this way.
